text:
Abstract
This study compares the scope and assay composition of Staphylococcus aureus data in two NCBI/EBI resources: GEO (processed gene expression studies) and ENA (raw sequencing runs). We resolved the organism to NCBI Taxonomy ID 1280, then queried GEO for Series (GSE) records overall and by assay terms (“RNA-Seq”, “Expression profiling by array”, “ChIP-Seq”). In parallel, we counted ENA runs for taxid 1280 overall and by controlled library_strategy (WGS, RNA-Seq, AMPLICON). Key findings: GEO holds 500 Series for S. aureus, including 93 with an RNA-seq term, 188 with “Expression profiling by array”, and 9 with “ChIP-Seq”. ENA holds 181,408 total runs for taxid 1280, including 171,172 WGS, 6,465 RNA-Seq, and 1,219 AMPLICON runs. We also inspected exemplar records returned in each query to confirm assay types and metadata fields. These results quantify the difference between curated expression matrices (GEO) and raw sequence data (ENA), providing practical guidance for analysis planning: ENA offers far broader raw sequencing coverage, while GEO concentrates a smaller set of processed expression studies suitable for downstream differential expression analyses.

I. Introduction
Background. Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive bacterial pathogen of clinical importance. For computational analyses, GEO provides processed expression datasets (e.g., counts or normalized matrices) suitable for expression-level inference, while ENA hosts raw sequencing runs enabling alignment, assembly, and primary QC.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. The relative sizes and assay composition of S. aureus data in GEO versus ENA had not been quantified in this comparison.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: quantify and compare the number and assay types of S. aureus records in GEO (Series) and ENA (runs). Hypothesis: ENA holds many more raw runs than GEO holds processed Series, and ENA’s assay mix is dominated by WGS.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We compared GEO Series counts (overall and by commonly queried assay terms) to ENA run counts (overall and by library_strategy) for Staphylococcus aureus. We used NCBI Taxonomy to confirm species and obtain the taxid for ENA queries.

Materials.
- NCBI Taxonomy via ncbi_taxonomy_lookup
- NCBI GEO via geo_search
- ENA via brc_ena_runs (BRC Analytics proxy) and brc_ena_search (controlled query to ENA Portal)

Procedures.
- ncbi_taxonomy_lookup:
  - arguments: {"query": "Staphylococcus aureus"}
- GEO Series counts (each returns total_count for the query):
  - geo_search {"organism":"Staphylococcus aureus","entry_type":"gse","max_results":1}
  - geo_search {"organism":"Staphylococcus aureus","term":"RNA-Seq","entry_type":"gse","max_results":1}
  - geo_search {"organism":"Staphylococcus aureus","term":"\"Expression profiling by array\"","entry_type":"gse","max_results":1}
  - geo_search {"organism":"Staphylococcus aureus","term":"ChIP-Seq","entry_type":"gse","max_results":1}
- ENA run counts:
  - brc_ena_runs {"taxonomy_id":"1280","limit":1} to obtain total_in_ena
  - brc_ena_search {"taxonomy_id":"1280","library_strategy":"WGS","limit":1} to obtain total_matching
  - brc_ena_search {"taxonomy_id":"1280","library_strategy":"RNA-Seq","limit":1} to obtain total_matching
  - brc_ena_search {"taxonomy_id":"1280","library_strategy":"AMPLICON","limit":1} to obtain total_matching

Statistical Analysis.
- GEO: Counts reported from the “total_count” field in geo_search responses for entry_type=gse. The query_translation note indicates NCBI’s rewriting of terms; we report the server-returned totals without adjustment. No deduplication was performed.
- ENA: Overall run count from brc_ena_runs “total_in_ena” for taxonomy_id=1280; assay-specific counts from brc_ena_search “total_matching” for library_strategy=WGS, RNA-Seq, AMPLICON. No deduplication was performed. Percentages were not computed; counts are reported as returned.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Overall counts for Staphylococcus aureus in GEO (Series) and ENA (runs)

| Resource | Scope | Count | Count Field |
|---|---|---:|---|
| GEO | Series (GSE) | 500 | total_count |
| ENA | Runs (taxid 1280) | 181,408 | total_in_ena |

Table 2. Assay-specific counts

| Resource | Assay category | Count | Query scope | Count Field |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GEO | RNA-Seq (term) | 93 | Series (GSE) | total_count |
| GEO | Expression profiling by array (term) | 188 | Series (GSE) | total_count |
| GEO | ChIP-Seq (term) | 9 | Series (GSE) | total_count |
| ENA | WGS (library_strategy) | 171,172 | Runs (tax_eq(1280)) | total_matching |
| ENA | RNA-Seq (library_strategy) | 6,465 | Runs (tax_eq(1280)) | total_matching |
| ENA | AMPLICON (library_strategy) | 1,219 | Runs (tax_eq(1280)) | total_matching |

Findings.
- GEO holds 500 Series for Staphylococcus aureus.
- GEO Series carrying the term “RNA-Seq” total 93. Series with “Expression profiling by array” total 188. Series with “ChIP-Seq” total 9.
- ENA holds 181,408 total runs for taxid 1280.
- ENA library_strategy counts: WGS 171,172; RNA-Seq 6,465; AMPLICON 1,219.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. ENA holds far more raw sequencing runs for Staphylococcus aureus than GEO holds processed expression Series. Within ENA, WGS dominates the assay composition, whereas GEO’s Series include both RNA-seq and array-based expression studies with smaller totals.

Context. The GEO results demonstrate curated expression study availability with experiment types visible in the Series metadata (returned examples confirm RNA-seq and array assays). ENA results quantify the breadth of raw data for S. aureus, with controlled library_strategy facets exposing the run-level assay composition.

Limitations.
- GEO counts depend on NCBI’s query translation. Term-based queries (“RNA-Seq”, “Expression profiling by array”, “ChIP-Seq”) reflect rewritten queries and free-text matching, not a controlled per-Series assay facet. The results are Series-level totals, not sample-level counts.
- ENA counts are run-level and use tax_eq(1280), which matches the species taxon (and its descendants) at submission time; they are not directly comparable to GEO Series counts.
- Only one record per query was returned for inspection; counts are from server-provided totals. No auditing of duplicates or cross-study overlaps was performed.

Conclusion & Future Directions. ENA provides extensive raw sequencing coverage of Staphylococcus aureus, dominated by WGS, suitable for genome-scale analyses. GEO offers a smaller but focused set of processed expression studies, useful for transcriptomic analyses without raw data processing. A next query worth running is to facet GEO Series by experiment_type using richer filters (e.g., fetching and parsing Series metadata across the full set) and to break down ENA runs by instrument, year, and host to profile sequencing trends.

References
[1] NCBI Taxonomy — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?term=Staphylococcus+aureus&retmax=50&retstart=0&sort=relevance&retmode=json&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
[2] NCBI Taxonomy — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?id=1280&retmode=xml&db=taxonomy&tool=fdea-ncbi-mcp&email=jonathangunti%40gmail.com
[3] NCBI GEO (Series, organism-only query) — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[4] NCBI GEO (Series, RNA-Seq term) — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[5] NCBI GEO (Series, “Expression profiling by array” term) — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[6] NCBI GEO (Series, ChIP-Seq term) — https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[7] BRC Analytics ENA proxy (taxonomy runs) — https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/1280
[8] ENA Portal (WGS library_strategy) — https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search
[9] ENA Portal (RNA-Seq library_strategy) — https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search
[10] ENA Portal (AMPLICON library_strategy) — https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI Taxonomy, NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), and the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA), with ENA access via BRC Analytics’ public proxy.
